Stage 2 of our journey · Synthetic test system: 450 wells

The hidden-truth test: can the model find a level it never saw?

In the test system we know the true water level at all times. The model learned from the first 150 days of noisy readings, then forecast the final 30 days. Compare its forecasts with the hidden truth, well by well.

What you can do here

Pick a type of well (for example "recharge dominated" or "sensor drift") or a specific well, and see its forecast set against the hidden truth.

Designed to be hard

Some wells were built to break models, such as sensors that slowly drift. No model can fix a drifting sensor, which is why we ask for calibration records.

What it proved

Given good readings, the model tracked the hidden truth to within about 0.3 m on average over 30 days. Compare approaches.

Decoder: what the labels on this page mean
Average error (MAE)
How far off the forecasts were, on average, in metres. Lower is better.
RMSE
Another error measure that punishes big misses more heavily.
Bias
A lean in one direction: + means forecasts were too deep on average, − too shallow.
80% coverage
How often the true level landed inside the shaded range. For an honest "80%" range it should be about 80%.

Interpretation: this page measures whether the statistical structure can recover the known synthetic system. It does not establish real-world Bengaluru accuracy; that requires the same inputs and holdout design on genuine wells.

Conditional-input test: the model receives actual future pumping, supply, demand and raw rain. This tests how it follows the level when those inputs are known. Rain delay is selected on days 121–150; final days 151–180 are used only for scoring. Nominal 80% bands are calibrated on the inner window; the coverage above is their measured final holdout coverage.

Borewell Forecast is a proof of concept for forecasting groundwater levels in Bengaluru borewells. Results are labelled by where the data came from: real pump data (15 days, July 2026), synthetic test system (450 simulated wells with a known answer) or digital twin (a physics-based simulation of the 579 wells over a year). Nothing here is yet a validated field forecast.
